scene: At Kadesh-barnea, returned scouts lay fresh grapes and figs before the Israelites. One scout points insistently toward the good hill country and a distant fortified town, while frightened families turn away toward their tents. Moses stands beside the scouts urging the people forward. The dominant action is the people's refusal to enter despite the good fruit; show the fruit, the pointing scout, and the turned-away families together in one grounded scene.
avoid: No enormous fantasy grapes, floating flashbacks, desert procession, or celebration of entering Canaan.

scene: An intentional two-part narrative painting with a restrained vertical division: on the left, Israelite travelers pay weighed silver pieces to local traders for water jars and grain beside the red hills of Seir, weapons lowered; on the right, farther north at a rocky river gorge, Israelite soldiers advance toward a defeated Amorite fortified settlement after Sihon opposed their passage. Make peaceful payment and the distinct later victory equally legible. These are separate stages of the journey, not one simultaneous event.
avoid: No attacking the traders, no coins with modern designs, no conflating Edom or Moab with Sihon's kingdom, no gore.

scene: In the conquered highland region of Bashan, Israelite men inspect an exceptionally long, broad iron bedstead, clearly a bed with a sleeping platform, dwarfed by its scale. The bed is the foreground visual emblem of King Og recalled in the chapter, not a reconstruction of where it was found. Beyond are formidable dark-stone walled towns now quiet. At one side Moses encourages Joshua, gesturing west toward the Jordan valley. Prioritize the unmistakable oversized iron bed and fortified Bashan.
avoid: Do not show a living fantasy giant, a bed being used as a chariot, Moses crossing the Jordan, or Moses dying; the death belongs to chapter 34.

scene: Israel stands at the foot of Horeb, listening in awe to a mountain burning with fire inside dark cloud. The mountain and its unfigured fire dominate the composition; families and children are seen from behind, small against the slopes. The crucial point is hearing without seeing any divine shape. Show fire, cloud, listeners, and empty hands; God's presence has no visible body or face.
avoid: No human silhouette in the fire, giant face in the sky, idol, golden calf, or Moses holding tablets as the main subject.

scene: Moses stands before Israel's assembled elders and families, presenting exactly two intact stone tablets side by side as he restates the covenant commands. The two tablets are prominent, their faces inscribed with rows of artistic ancient Hebrew-style marks. The crowd listens attentively; distant dark mountain slopes and a faint glow recall Horeb without competing with the tablets. The image must read immediately as two covenant tablets being taught to Israel.
avoid: No broken tablets, golden calf, dramatic tablet smashing, modern stone monuments, or invented numbered commandment text.

scene: A close, intimate Israelite household scene: a parent seated at a simple doorway teaches God's commands to two attentive children, one child repeating the lesson with a hand over the heart. The parent's finger rests on a small teaching scroll, while the other hand indicates the home's doorpost bearing a small reminder with its writing turned away. A second parent listens nearby. Warm morning light reaches the family, and a path outside suggests teaching during daily travel. Make the teaching interaction, children, heart gesture, and doorpost visible at thumbnail size. Depict the household instruction commanded in the chapter, not Moses giving another public speech.
avoid: No floating heart icon, glowing anatomical heart, generic praying man, modern classroom or printed Bible; do not turn this into a tablets-on-a-mountain scene.

scene: Israelites dismantle an abandoned pagan shrine: two men pull down a carved sacred pillar while another breaks apart an empty altar. Splintered wooden idol pieces lie beside a small controlled fire. Families stand at a respectful distance, facing away from the rejected shrine toward their community. The dominant visual action is removing idolatrous worship as a people set apart, with strong, clear silhouettes.
avoid: No golden calf, no destruction of the tabernacle, no attacked civilians, no gore, no suggestion of a modern ethnic group.

scene: In the wilderness at dawn, an Israelite adult kneels to gather small pale manna flakes into a shallow bowl, then offers some to a child. Worn but serviceable sandals are visible beside the kneeling figure. The poor stony ground occupies the foreground; a distant fertile valley with springs and grain recalls the promised abundance. Manna in the open hands is the sharpest visual focus: dependence on God's provision before prosperity.
avoid: No giant loaf, bread falling from the sky, supernatural face, affluent banquet, or rock being struck; this is the reminder of manna, not a separate miracle narrative.

scene: Moses has just cast down the two covenant tablets: two clearly broken slabs and fresh fragments lie at his feet, his hands still lowered from the act. Behind him a golden calf on a low pedestal and halted celebrants identify the people's rebellion. His expression is grief and urgency rather than triumph. The large broken tablet pieces retain partial rows of engraved Hebrew-style marks. The tablets and calf must both be unmistakable, with the shattered stone dominating the foreground.
avoid: No intact tablets presented to a listening crowd, no new tablets placed in a chest, no graphic violence.

scene: Moses carefully lowers exactly two NEW intact stone tablets into an open acacia-wood chest in the foreground. Nearby, a member of Israel offers food and a cloak to a travel-worn foreigner and a widow with a child. Both actions belong in one clear teaching composition: covenant renewal at the center, wholehearted obedience expressed as compassion at the side. The intact tablet faces bear artistic engraved Hebrew-style marks. The simple wooden chest, intact tablets, bread, and cloak are readable visual cues.
avoid: No shattered tablets, golden calf, literal surgery, anatomical heart, bleeding, or a jewel-encrusted fantasy treasure chest.

scene: A hillside grain field receives visible soft rain from clouds opening in warm light. An Israelite farming family lifts open hands among wet grain, with olive trees and a vineyard on the adjoining terraces. At the far edge, a smaller parched hillside under a closed bronze-colored sky provides a restrained visual contrast for withheld rain. Rain touching grain and the grateful family's response are dominant.
avoid: No flood, ark, rainbow, manna gathering, or equal-sized dramatic war panorama; keep this distinct from chapter 28's national blessings and curses.

scene: Several small family groups approach ONE central worship courtyard along paths converging from surrounding hills. They bring baskets, jars, and a firstborn lamb toward a single altar, with a modest tent sanctuary beyond. One household shares a joyful meal inside the court. This is an instructional visualization of the chosen place, not an identification of a specific later site. The converging paths and one focal sanctuary must be visually obvious.
avoid: No multiple competing altars, Solomon's temple, church, mosque, city skyline, or scattered mountain shrines.

scene: A persuasive would-be prophet holds out a small foreign idol, beckoning an Israelite household to follow it. The family's elder firmly raises an open palm in refusal and guides the children away. The idol remains in the deceiver's hand, never revered by the family. A clear face-to-face choice, the extended idol, and the refusing palm dominate the scene.
avoid: No prophet like Moses being welcomed, no generic argument without an idol, no executions, no stage magic, no caricature of another contemporary faith.

scene: At a village storehouse, a farmer separates ONE full grain basket from a clearly countable group of TEN matching baskets: nine together and the tenth being handed toward a Levite and a widow with a child. Oil and wine jars sit behind them. Sheep grazing at the margin supply a quiet clean-animal cue without becoming a zoo. The tenth share and provision for others are the focus, with every basket completely visible.
avoid: No money plate, coins, modern church offering, one firstfruit basket at an altar (chapter 26), or eleven baskets.

scene: At an open household gate, a former servant leaves freely with a bundle of grain, a jar, and a sheep supplied by the household. The householder offers an open-handed farewell and releases a rolled debt document into the recipient's hand, with its writing concealed. Relief and dignity are visible on both faces. The open gate and generous departure supplies make this clearly a release, not a sale or an arrest.
avoid: No prison chains, whip, auction, fleeing captive, modern debt notice, or empty-handed departure.

scene: A deliberate triptych, three balanced adjacent painted scenes, visually distinct and NOT simultaneous: first, a family at a modest evening Passover meal with flat unleavened bread; second, pilgrims joyfully carrying wheat sheaves and freewill gifts at the Feast of Weeks; third, a family sharing harvest food beneath a leafy temporary booth at Tabernacles. Keep the three principal objects large: flat bread, wheat sheaves, leafy booth. No text or labels appear in any panel.
avoid: No panel labels, modern holidays, Christmas symbols, temple skyline, or one generic banquet that hides the three feasts.

scene: An imagined future Israelite king in modest royal clothing sits at a simple table COPYING the law by hand onto a scroll under the supervision of a Levitical priest. A restrained crown rests beside the scroll, lower than the writing hand. The king leans over the law with humility, while the priest holds the exemplar. Frame hands, reed pen, two scrolls and crown clearly; writing faces away so no fabricated scripture is readable.
avoid: No enthroned tyrant, battle scene, piles of gold, many horses, modern codex Bible, or royal proclamation to a crowd.

scene: Moses addresses a listening Israelite assembly with an open-handed gesture toward the people. Behind and beyond him, a second humble Israelite teacher appears as a softly separated future-facing narrative vignette, speaking God's message to attentive hearers with open hands and no idol. This is an explicitly illustrative promise of a prophet raised from among their own people, not a literal meeting of the two men. Contrast the welcomed teacher here with chapter 13's rejected deceiver.
avoid: No fortune-teller, crystal ball, idol, angel wings, divine face, halo, or claim that a specific costume is prescribed by this chapter.

scene: A frightened woodcutter carrying an AXE HANDLE WITH ITS HEAD MISSING reaches an open stone city gate, where sober elders receive him and hold back an angry pursuer outside. In the distance two more refuge towns sit along prepared roads, small secondary cues to the three cities. Show the broken tool, open gate, protective elder and arriving woodcutter prominently. The scene conveys protection while the case is heard.
avoid: No bloody weapon, intentional murderer celebrating escape, modern courtroom, execution, or closed gate barring the refugee.

scene: Before any fighting begins, a linen-clad priest stands facing rows of Israelite soldiers and encourages them with a calm raised hand. Their shields are lowered as they listen; one apprehensive soldier quietly takes the path home at the side. Fruit trees remain standing intact near a distant walled town. The priest speaking courage to the assembled army is the main action, not charging soldiers.
avoid: No Moses with tablets, visible deity leading troops, blazing fruit orchards, active slaughter, or modern weapons.

scene: In an uncultivated valley beside a running brook, city elders perform the handwashing declaration for an unsolved killing. Their extended hands and poured water dominate the foreground; a young heifer lies still nearby, its neck and any injury fully concealed by its natural position and tall reeds. A priest witnesses the solemn declaration. The stream, elders washing, and unobtrusive heifer identify the prescribed ceremony. Show no victim and no act of killing.
avoid: No bloody sacrifice, altar, burning animal, graphic injury, calf worship, or generic cattle watering scene.

scene: On a flat-roofed Israelite stone house, a builder carefully lays the final stones of a substantial waist-high protective parapet. A family stands safely INSIDE the completed part of the wall, with the steep drop beyond clearly visible. On the road below, a neighbor leads a stray sheep back toward its owner as a small supporting action. The continuous roof safety wall and the worker building it must be the unmistakable main subject.
avoid: No roof without a parapet, child balancing on the edge, falling person, modern guardrail, or generic house construction.

scene: A neatly ordered Israelite military camp is seen from just outside its marked perimeter at sunrise. In the foreground a fully clothed soldier uses a small digging tool to cover a shallow sanitation pit OUTSIDE the camp; there is no exposed body or visible waste. Behind him, clean paths separate orderly tents and a water basin. The camp boundary and outside digging action must be clear, conveying practical care for a holy camp.
avoid: No toileting, nakedness, excrement, divine figure walking between tents, modern latrine, or generic army camp without the outside-camp action.

scene: At sunset beside a harvested field, a landowner pays a poor laborer's daily wages into his open hand. Close behind, a widow, a child and a foreign traveler gather a visibly LEFT-BEHIND sheaf and olives, with no one driving them away. A smaller quiet doorway scene at the far margin shows a woman receiving a rolled separation document, acknowledging the chapter's opening regulations without dominating the wider theme of protection. Prioritize wages paid before sunset and gleaning left for vulnerable people.
avoid: No wedding celebration, romantic reconciliation, forced reunion, eviction violence, modern currency, or a divorce-only image omitting the chapter's social justice laws.

scene: At the city gate, a widow holds up the sandal she has removed from her deceased husband's brother, whose one bare foot is visible. The man stands with a downcast, refusing posture while seated elders witness the public refusal of family responsibility. Focus tightly enough that the sandal, bare foot, widow and witnesses are all unmistakable. A merchant's balanced scales in the distance may quietly recall honest measures without distracting.
avoid: No wedding, romantic couple, shoe exchange by two men (a different scene from Ruth), bodily humiliation, or spitting close-up.

scene: A grateful farmer kneels while a priest receives ONE woven basket filled with the first ripe figs, grapes and grain, then lowers it beside a simple altar. The farmer's family stands reverently behind him, his open hand on his chest as he recounts the people's deliverance and entry into the land. The single abundant firstfruits basket and thankful bow are prominent, distinct from the ten-basket tithe scene.
avoid: No ten baskets, gold treasure, generic harvest market, sacrifice of a child, or later monumental temple.

scene: On Mount Ebal, large upright stones freshly coated with pale plaster dominate the foreground. A scribe carefully writes the LAW on the plaster, his hand and stone angled so the script is not legible. Nearby stands a low altar made of rough UNCUT stones. Across the valley groups of Israelites stand on the two opposing mountain slopes while Levites lead the covenant response. White plastered standing stones, rough altar, and opposite gathered slopes make this distinct.
avoid: Do not call the stone inscription only curses; no tablet-shaped monument held by Moses, polished masonry altar, modern plaque, or invented readable scripture.

scene: A solemn paired panorama of covenant consequences. One half shows a settled town with full grain baskets, thriving fields and healthy flocks under gentle rain. The other half shows cracked ground, empty baskets, a besieged damaged town, and a small distant line of exiles departing. Repeat the basket shape on both sides to make fullness versus loss immediate. Give the warning side substantial visual weight; this chapter is not only a prosperity promise.
avoid: No happy-only harvest, gore, modern war equipment, literal heaven-versus-hell diagram, forked road as main subject, or unqualified promise of personal wealth.

scene: On the plains of Moab, the entire community gathers around Moses and the openly presented covenant scroll: elders, women, children, a foreign woodcutter with a bundle, and a water carrier with jars. Their attentive faces and varied daily roles are prominent in a wide semicircle. The revealed teaching is illuminated in the foreground while distant heights remain veiled by cloud, a subtle reminder that hidden things belong to God. The main message is everyone entering the covenant, not a magical secret.
avoid: No locked treasure chest, mystery key, glowing riddle, hooded occult figure, or assembly made only of male warriors.

scene: An explicitly symbolic teaching landscape: an Israelite parent and child stand at a fork in the road, then take a deliberate step together toward a sunlit, living grove and cultivated land. The alternative path leads into dry, lifeless ground. Moses stands beside the junction with an open scroll, directing attention toward life. Make the actual choosing step and the joined hands visually central. This visual metaphor illustrates the stated choice, not a claim that Moses staged a literal road ceremony.
avoid: No cartoon arrows, floating life/death icons, skeleton, burning hell, mere scenic fork with no person choosing, or duplication of chapter 28's national panorama.

scene: Outside the Tent of Meeting, aged Moses encourages Joshua before the gathered people. Beside them, a Levitical priest receives a finished scroll to preserve as a witness, while a small attentive group repeats the song Moses has taught. The chapter's distinctive combination is the successor, the entrusted written witness, and people learning together. Keep Moses, Joshua and the handed-over scroll large and clear; no floating music symbols.
avoid: No Joshua crossing the Jordan yet, Moses dying, scroll inside the ark (the law book is placed beside it), or solitary singer omitting the handover.

scene: An explicitly poetic illustration of the Song of Moses: Moses recites to listening Israel at the base of a massive enduring rock formation. Above a rocky ledge, an eagle spreads its wings protectively over its young, clearly a natural eagle used as the chapter's metaphor of care. The steadfast rock and protective eagle dominate the composition; below them a few people turn away toward a small distant idol, hinting at the song's warning about ingratitude. The singing is sober and instructive, not a festival.
avoid: No water gushing from a struck rock, no supernatural face in stone, no rescue by an invented giant bird, no musical notes, no image consisting only of Moses writing.

scene: Aged Moses stands on a low rise with both hands extended in a final benediction over clustered tribal households. Distinct small groups of families, shepherds, farmers and Levites gather in a broad semicircle, with tents behind and morning light over the land. A shepherd's flock, a farmer's harvest and the Levites' plain sacred service garments give varied blessings concrete form. Moses blessing the gathered tribes is the unmistakable focal action.
avoid: No king being crowned, no military briefing, no fabricated tribal emblems or named banners, no death scene; do not invent a separate blessing of Simeon, which is not named in this chapter.

scene: Moses stands ALONE on the summit of Mount Nebo, seen in three-quarter profile with weathered face, white beard and wooden staff, looking west over the Jordan valley toward the fertile promised land and distant Jericho. His feet remain on the rocky Moab side; the river below is visibly uncrossed. The mood is peaceful farewell, with the land filling most of the wide composition. Depict the final view before his death, not a speculative scene of his burial.
avoid: No Joshua beside him on the summit, Moses entering Canaan, visible divine figure, corpse, known grave monument, or later Jerusalem temple.
